ing: dried fermented yogurt; or use 4 cups plain whole-milk yogurt
st: Break the jameed into pieces and soak it in warm water to cover for at least 2 hours. If using yogurt instead, skip this step.
Put the lamb and onion in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water. Bring to a boil and skim off the grey foam that rises.
Reduce the heat to low, add [[1 tsp]] salt, cover and simmer until the lamb is very tender.
Blend the soaked jameed with [[1 cup]] of its soaking water until smooth, then strain. (For the yogurt version, whisk [[4 cups]] yogurt until smooth.)
Remove the lamb from the pot and set aside. Strain the broth, then stir the jameed liquid into [[3 cups]] of the broth in a clean pot.
Heat the sauce gently over low heat, stirring constantly in one direction so it does not split. Return the lamb to it and simmer for 15 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] ghee in a pot, stir in the rice and turmeric, then add [[3.5 cups]] hot water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cover and cook on low until the water is absorbed.
Toast the almonds in [[2 tbsp]] ghee in a small pan over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes.
Lay the flatbread on a large platter and moisten with a few ladlefuls of the sauce. Pile the rice on top, then arrange the lamb over the rice.
Scatter the almonds on top and serve with a bowl of warm jameed sauce on the side for pouring.
Put the chicken, onion, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[4 cups]] water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the chicken is cooked through (165°F/74°C). Save the broth.
Salt the eggplant slices lightly with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and let them sit for 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat about [[0.5 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the eggplant, cauliflower and potatoes in batches until golden, then drain on paper towels.
Brush the bottom of a heavy pot with oil and lay the tomato slices in a circle. Arrange the chicken, then the fried vegetables, in tight layers on top.
Mix the drained rice with [[2 tsp]] allspice, turmeric, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and pepper. Spread it evenly over the vegetables.
Pour [[3 cups]] of the hot chicken broth gently over the rice. Press down lightly so everything is submerged.
Bring to a boil, cover tightly, then cook on low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone.
Turn off the heat and let the pot rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Place a large round platter over the pot. Holding both firmly with oven mitts, flip it over, wait a minute, then lift the pot off slowly.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Rub the chicken with [[2 tbsp]] oil, [[1 tbsp]] sumac, allspice, cinnamon, [[1 tsp]] salt, pepper and lemon juice. Let it sit while you cook the onions.
Cook the onions in [[0.25 cup]] oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat, stirring often, until very soft and golden.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] sumac and [[1 tsp]] salt and cook 2 more minutes. Set aside.
Roast the chicken on a baking sheet until the skin is browned and the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C).
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes, shaking the pan often.
Spread half the onions over a baking sheet, lay the flatbread on top, and spread the remaining onions over the bread. Warm in the oven for 5 minutes.
Place the chicken on the bread, drizzle with the pan juices, scatter the pine nuts over and serve right away.
Mix the baharat, turmeric, salt, pepper, garlic and oil into a paste. Rub it all over the lamb and chicken, and let it marinate in the fridge for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Home ovens stand in for the traditional underground pit.
Layer the lamb in the bottom of a large deep roasting pan, then add the onions and carrots.
Add the potatoes, tomatoes and [[1 cup]] water. Place the chicken on top.
Cover the pan tightly with foil so the steam stays in.
Bake until the lamb is very tender and falls from the bone. Add 20 minutes if the lamb is not soft yet.
Uncover and bake 20 more minutes to brown the chicken. Check the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Serve everything piled on a big platter with the pan juices spooned over.

ing: peeled, soaked overnight; or use more chickpeas
st: Drain the soaked chickpeas and fava beans well and pat them dry. They must stay raw, not cooked.
Put the beans, onion, garlic and parsley in a food processor. Pulse until the mix looks like coarse crumbs, scraping down the sides.
Add cumin, coriander, baking soda and salt and pulse again briefly. Squeeze a bit: it should hold together.
Cover and chill the mixture for 30 minutes.
Shape into small balls or flat patties about the size of a walnut, pressing firmly. Roll in sesame seeds if you like.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry 5 or 6 pieces at a time until deep golden brown and crisp, about 3 minutes, turning once.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm in flatbread with tahini sauce, pickles and tomatoes.
Put the chickpeas in a pot, cover with water and bring to a simmer for 10 minutes. This makes them softer and the hummus smoother.
Meanwhile, blend the tahini and lemon juice in a food processor for 1 minute until pale and thick.
Add the garlic, cumin and salt and blend for 30 seconds.
Drain the warm chickpeas and add them to the processor. Blend for 3 to 4 minutes, scraping the sides now and then.
With the machine running, slowly add the ice water, [[1 tbsp]] at a time, until the hummus is creamy and fluffy. Taste and add more salt or lemon if you like.
Spread in a shallow bowl, making a swirl in the middle. Drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with paprika. Serve with warm bread.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and chili and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Raise the heat to medium-high and let them sizzle, stirring now and then.
Lower the heat and cook, uncovered, until the tomatoes break down and the juices thicken, about 15 minutes.
Taste and add more salt or chili if needed.
Serve warm from the pan with flatbread for scooping, often alongside fried eggs or hummus.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrots until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and turmeric and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils and [[6 cups]] water. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Reduce the heat, partly cover and simmer until the lentils and carrots are completely soft.
Blend the soup with an immersion blender until smooth. Add a splash of water if it is too thick.
Stir in the salt and lemon juice. Taste and adjust.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and bread.

ing: shredded; or half mozzarella, half ricotta
optional, for the traditional red top
st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Butter a 10-inch round baking pan.
Make the syrup: simmer the sugar and water for 10 minutes. Stir in the lemon juice, simmer 1 minute, then add the rose water and cool.
Shred the kataifi dough into short pieces with your hands or scissors, then rub with the melted butter until every strand is coated.
Press two thirds of the dough into the pan, firmly and evenly, making a base with a small rim up the sides.
Cover with the cheese, leaving a small border at the edge.
Top with the remaining dough and press down gently to seal in the cheese.
Bake until golden brown on top, about 35 minutes.
Pour the cooled syrup evenly over the hot knafeh. Let it soak for 5 minutes.
Scatter the pistachios over the top. Cut into squares and serve warm while the cheese is still stretchy.
Mix both flours and salt, add the oil and stir in the warm water gradually until you have a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest 45 minutes.
Divide into 10 small balls, dust with flour and let them rest 15 minutes more.
Heat a large wok turned upside down, or a flat skillet, over high heat until very hot, about 3 minutes.
Roll or stretch one ball over the back of your hands into a round as thin as paper, about 14 inches wide.
Lay it over the hot dome and cook 30 seconds until blistered with brown spots. Peel off, fold in quarters and stack under a cloth to stay soft.
nt: Cooked on a very hot dry griddle
Best swap: use a flipped wok or cast iron skillet instead of a saj dome; same high heat.
